fear_greed.commentary: The index hasn't updated since Friday's close, when it sat in extreme fear at 21, barely above Thursday's 20 and down from 22 a week ago and 33 a month ago.

markets.summary: Markets were closed for the weekend, so the table and breadth still reflect Friday's Oct. 23 close: the S&P 500 at 7,623.68 (-0.52%), the Dow at 52,215.16 (-1.23%) and the Nasdaq at 25,955.34 (-0.21%), with the S&P and Nasdaq down two straight weeks on the AI and tech selloff while the Dow posted a third weekly gain. Small caps eased Friday, with the Russell 2000 at 2,775.90, and the 10-year Treasury yield sat near 4.99%; gold futures ($4,007.90) and silver ($53.71) are down for the year and below their 40-week averages. Sunday evening, stock futures edged higher (S&P 500 futures up about 0.1%) and oil pulled back from six-month highs, with WTI near $101, after President Trump said there would be no strike on Iran that day. This week brings the Fed's meeting starting Tuesday with a decision Wednesday, earnings from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, and Q3 GDP and September PCE inflation on Thursday.

stories.headline: Musk says SpaceX closed $40 billion in GPU debt financing, predicts neocloud shakeout
stories.summary: Musk said the mostly callable debt funds GPUs arriving in the first half of 2027 and warned that tight credit will force failures among smaller AI cloud providers, adding SpaceX won't buy any of them.

stories.headline: SPCX rises overnight as another IPO lockup tranche expires
stories.summary: Shares rose nearly 1% late Sunday after Friday's close of $147.49, while up to 328.4 million more shares become eligible to trade Monday after a lockup expired Saturday.

stories.headline: Wall Street weighs SpaceX as a possible fifth hyperscaler and Tesla tie-up
stories.summary: Analysts are sizing up SpaceX's AI compute business after its earnings beat, with Musk projecting annual recurring revenue of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027.

stories.headline: Nvidia and Firebird expand Kazakhstan AI build-out
stories.summary: Firebird secured a U.S. export license for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs and began building its first phase in Ekibastuz, with commercial operations slated for Q3 2027 and later Vera Rubin deployments.

stories.headline: Huang puts Nvidia's AI agent software license at about $2,000 per GPU a year
stories.summary: Huang said software licensing will become a major part of Nvidia's business, though the company hasn't said which products the fee covers or when it would apply.

headlines.headline: U.S. stock futures edge higher after bruising tech losses; Fed, earnings on tap
headlines.summary: Futures steadied Sunday evening after two straight losing weeks for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, with a Fed meeting and big tech earnings ahead.

headlines.headline: Oil pulls back from six-month highs as Trump says no Iran strike today
headlines.summary: Brent fell about 1.6% to near $115 and WTI about 2% to near $101 Sunday night, while CENTCOM said Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes remain clear.

weather.summary: An upper low crossing the Four Corners keeps subtropical moisture flowing into the southern Rockies and southern High Plains, with a slight risk of flash flooding there tonight easing to marginal Monday. A low forming over the central High Plains brings 1 to locally 2 inches of rain to the northern Plains and upper Midwest Monday, with wet snow in the higher central and northern Rockies and from western South Dakota into central North Dakota, while heavy rain continues along Florida's east coast and a Pacific system soaks the Northwest into Idaho.
